transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-06
Start time: 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood - AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood - SE), Luis Romero (Redwood - Solutions), Cara Ito (Redwood - Partner Ops); Aisha Khan (CedarBridge - Head Partnerships), Tom Grady (Channel Ops), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect), Evan Liu (Procurement), Marco Reyes (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Quick partner intro between Redwood and CedarBridge. Primary focus: reseller/channel model, capacity/SLAs for dedicated pools, pilot scoping for hybrid private deployments, security baseline (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and technical validation items (throughput, kv cache, batching). Agreed to run a short baseline and share onboarding materials; several follow-ups identified.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the channel team. Quick round-robin?
[00:10] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha here, Head of Partnerships at CedarBridge. We're excited to explore a reseller-style collaboration.
[00:15] Tom Grady: Tom, channel ops, we'll handle GTM.
[00:18] Jonah Patel: Jonah, Redwood SE, I'll pick up the technical bits and run the bench stuff.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Priya, Cloud Architect. We'll be evaluating network, VPC peering, and on-prem options.
[00:28] Evan Liu: Evan, procurement — hi.
[00:30] Marco Reyes: Marco, SRE, I'll be looking at limits, observability hooks.

[00:35] Maya Chen: Cool. The goal for today is twofold: 1) high level partner model and what CedarBridge needs to resell or white-label Redwood inference; 2) quick technical alignment — what's required to run a pilot, what SLAs we can promise, and any security blockers.
[00:50] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. We want to know how Redwood handles dedicated capacity for partners, and if there's a private deployment path for regulated clients. A lot of our customers ask for both — a hosted first, then private option.
[01:02] Jonah Patel: Yep. We have three deployment modes — hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The Dedicated pools are the typical reseller-friendly path because you can commit capacity and we can expose a routing policy so you can route partner traffic. Sorry, uh our docs call it Redwood Dedicated, sometimes folks say 'Redwood Dedicata' in notes — minor typo in some transcripts.
[01:20] Priya Nair: On the Dedicated option, what's the typical latency envelope and how does bursting work? We primarily care about tail latency for chat workloads — 95th percentile under a second ideally.
[01:32] Jonah Patel: Right. Latency depends on model and sequence length — with modern open models we can hit sub-400ms for short chat prompts on a well-provisioned pool. For chat that needs context we use KV cache and continuous batching; that helps keep costs down while meeting latency SLOs. Bursting is supported via autoscale policies but bursts can move to compatible model variants if short-term capacity is full.
[01:51] Marco Reyes: When you say compatible variants — that's quantized models often? How much quality delta are we looking at? Some of our customers won't accept big quality drop.
[01:58] Jonah Patel: Great question. We maintain graded variants: float16 FP16, int8 quantized, and tuned quantized variants. Quantization can be almost transparent for many tasks; for very sensitive NLU/regression tasks you'll see variance. We also support rollouts and can A/B test during pilot.
[02:12] Tom Grady: For reseller margins — high level — are you offering partner discounts on committed capacity? And do you allow bundle pricing for private deployments?
[02:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we have channel pricing tiers tied to commit size and term. We also have an enterprise Private license model (platform fee + support) and channel margins are negotiable based on volume. I'll share the reseller onboarding deck with the margin matrix after the call.
[02:33] Aisha Khan: Excellent. Security — we need SOC2 Type II, SSO (SAML), RBAC, and audit logs for customers. Also KMS integration is essential.
[02:44] Luis Romero: Redwood supports SOC2 and has KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For hosted we have tenant encryption and audit granularity; for Private deployments you run your own KMS. There's an audit logs pipeline and we can surface logs to your SIEM.
[02:58] Priya Nair: On network: can we do VPC peering and limit egress? Some customers have strict egress policies.
[03:04] Jonah Patel: Yes, Private can be customer-managed networking with VPC peering. For Dedicated we offer VPC endpoints and IP allowlists; egress cost controls are possible and we can publish expected egress metrics in the onboarding doc.
[03:15] Marco Reyes: Observability — how granular are traces? We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards.
[03:22] Luis Romero: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-model dashboards, traces and error analysis. There's also hooks for custom tracing if you want to forward spans to an APM.
[03:32] Aisha Khan: Okay, on pilot scoping: CedarBridge wants to run a 2-week baseline with a small dedicated pool to validate latency and cost on our sample workloads. We'll need a pricing quote and an SLA during pilot.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Sounds doable. Typical pilots are 1-4 weeks. For the baseline we recommend sending a representative workload (Priya, Marco) — sequence length distribution, QPS targets, and expected concurrency. We'll run both a straight-hosted run and a small Redwood Dedicated pool to compare unit economics.
[03:58] Priya Nair: We'll provide a workload and example prompts. Also, we need to test an on-prem adapter for a couple regulated customers — is there a supported package?
[04:06] Jonah Patel: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped installs but it'll require a security review and an enterprise license. For initial scoping we can do VPC/private path which is faster.
[04:15] Evan Liu: Procurement question — typical lead time on Dedicated commits and billing terms?
[04:20] Maya Chen: Standard is 30-60 days for contract negotiation. Billing can be monthly or annual, and we offer committed discounts for annual terms. We can share contract templates and the reseller addendum.
[04:30] Aisha Khan: Competitors — our customers also evaluate Aurora Compute and NimbusGrid; we'll need a clear differentiation deck on performance and cost.
[04:38] Luis Romero: We'll share recent benchmarks and a cost comparison. Note that bench numbers vary by model and sequence length; we'll include notes on kernel selection and batching so it's apples-to-apples.
[04:50] Marco Reyes: For the bench — what telemetry/logs will you provide? We need token-level latency histograms and traces for failed requests.
[04:57] Jonah Patel: We'll provide logs, token latency histograms, top-k failure reasons, and per-model breakdowns. For pilot we're happy to establish an S3 bucket or secure share for logs.
[05:08] Tom Grady: GTM — how do channel leads engage for co-marketing? We'll want joint logos, case studies, and maybe an SDK integration to make onboarding smoother.
[05:16] Cara Ito: Partner ops handles co-marketing; we can provide a partner portal, partner badges, and a joint launch checklist. We'll also offer sandbox API keys for your pre-sales engineers.
[05:26] Aisha Khan: Good, that's important. Also, what’s the support model during pilot — dedicated TAM?
[05:31] Luis Romero: For pilots above a threshold we assign a Solutions Engineer and an onboarding TAM. For larger pilots we can include a short-term SLA boost.
[05:39] Priya Nair: Are there any known pitfalls for on-prem installs (networking, GPU drivers)?
[05:44] Jonah Patel: Common items: driver/kernel mismatches, CUDA/ROCm versions, and NTP/time sync. We'll provide a checklist. Also, model compilation and kernel selection can take extra time for obscure hardware.
[05:55] Aisha Khan: Ok, that's helpful.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Quick recap / next steps: 1) Maya to send reseller onboarding deck + pricing worksheet; 2) Priya/Marco to share sample workload and network constraints; 3) Jonah to provision a small benchmark cluster and run KV/prefix cache tests; 4) schedule pilot scoping call w/ sales+engineering week of 7/16. Anything missing?
[06:18] Tom Grady: Can you also send a short redacted benchmark report comparing a 4k token chat flow across float16 vs int8? That helps internal PMs.
[06:26] Jonah Patel: Sure, we'll do a short comparison. Note that int8 numbers depend on quantization profile but we can give a demonstrative run.
[06:32] Evan Liu: I'll expect a procurement starter pack and an estimate for a 3-month pilot spend.
[06:38] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the follow-up.
[06:41] Aisha Khan: Great. Appreciate the time.
[06:44] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and set meetings.
[06:50] (meeting ends)

Call artifacts referenced: reseller_onboarding_deck.pdf (to be shared), pilot_benchmark_template.xlsx (to be shared), SOC2_summary_and_kms_integration.pdf (link forthcoming).

Recap (auto): Agreed pilot: 1) CedarBridge to provide workloads and constraints; 2) Redwood to run dedicated baseline and share logs; 3) security sync between teams; 4) deck + pricing to be shared. Action items recorded above.
